112  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

"He whispered as he looked down in her eyes,
'As he whispered as she turned away unsafely
Like the list of sunset skies.'

She said in sweet character,
'A good boy you must be.'
He softly wiped away his tears
Like the mist of sunset skies.

His face, with deep emotion,
Grew pale and wan and lame,
And he was seen by some and more,
And he was sad the same."

"Exhibitions" and "Levees."—Savoy made most of its own entertainment, as traveling shows and concerts came to Sherman or Bonham but not to smaller towns in the region. The types of local entertainment were mostly open programs and the exhibition affairs of the literary societies. The "exhibition" was one week of "showing off" similar to Commencement Exercises of longer duration; there was a program each night. Musicals, debates, speeches, orations, plays, "exercises" in one quarter, there was always the large family picture album (elaborate in plush or embossed, with music box), and at the exhibition the class walked in with their partner. In the students' language, they "spoke their pieces" and came upon the rostrum with their platform eloquence. The citizens came to the exhibitions with arm loads of lovely bouquets to offer compliments to their friends, and the group frequently demanded renditions by those who could sing, play an instrument, or recite. Eulogies and bouquets were thrown to the "rostrum."

Resolved that the following were debated at exhibitions with literary, historical, and ethical problems as well as with current, political, or local issues. One of the typical debates was: Resolved that the execution of Mary, Queen of Scots, was fair.

¹The Platonian Messenger, op. cit. Vol. II, No. 4, April 1, 1886.
